reasoning: The core problem and the exact proposed method are addressed by Lanham et al. (2023), "Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning" (Anthropic, arXiv:2307.13702), which applies precisely the three proposed interventions — truncation/early-answering, corruption (adding mistakes), and paraphrasing/replacement — measures how often the final answer is unchanged (the "causal-bypass rate"), and breaks this down across 8 multiple-choice NLP tasks (including arithmetic and commonsense) and model sizes, finding large cross-task variation in how much models condition on the CoT (inverse scaling of faithfulness). The "decorative vs. load-bearing CoT" framing is also already published (arXiv:2603.22816 on "decorative chain-of-thought" and arXiv:2510.24941 on "true vs. decorative thinking steps"), and counterfactual perturbation is a well-established category in the faithfulness literature (FaithCoT-Bench arXiv:2510.04040; survey arXiv:2509.03871). The only delta — running the established battery on a single small open instruct model (Qwen2.5-7B/Llama-3.1-8B) — is a replication on a new model rather than a novel contribution, which is why this is largely_addressed rather than fully already_solved.

evidence.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (Lanham et al., 2023)
evidence.summary: Directly applies truncation/early-answering, adding-mistakes (corruption), and paraphrasing interventions to CoT and measures whether the final answer changes, across 8 multiple-choice NLP tasks and model sizes. Finds models often ignore their CoT, with strong cross-task and inverse-scaling variation — operationally identical to the proposed causal-bypass-rate study by task type.

evidence.title: The illusion of reasoning: step-level evaluation reveals decorative chain-of-thought in frontier language models
evidence.summary: Explicitly distinguishes 'decorative' (answer-irrelevant) from 'load-bearing' CoT via step removal and measures necessity across tasks/models, matching the proposal's decorative-vs-load-bearing framing.

evidence.title: Can Aha Moments Be Fake? Identifying True and Decorative Thinking Steps in Chain-of-Thought
evidence.summary: Identifies 'decorative' vs causally-important thinking steps by checking whether the answer changes when steps are altered — the same decorative/load-bearing distinction the proposal targets.

evidence.title: FaithCoT-Bench: Benchmarking Instance-Level Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
evidence.summary: Survey/benchmark categorizing CoT faithfulness methods into counterfactual perturbation (remove/corrupt steps, force early answers and check if prediction changes), logit-based, and LLM-judge — establishing the proposed intervention battery as a known, standard methodology.

evidence.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Trustworthiness in Reasoning with Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Survey describing counterfactual perturbation of reasoning steps and checking final-answer change as a standard CoT-faithfulness measurement, confirming the problem is well-covered.

evidence.title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps (Tutek et al., 2025)
evidence.summary: Measures whether removing/unlearning reasoning steps changes the prediction to quantify causal importance of CoT, a close analog to the proposed truncate/corrupt causal-bypass measurement.
